raw.question: Shape of X-Forwarded-For as the API receives it in production behind Railway's edge (WP12 batch 4 prerequisite; incident docs/incidents/2026-11-05-client-ip-identity-collapse.md).
raw.method: Address-free measurement shipped in strale-io/strale#915 (deployed a7b094f1, 2026-11-05 ~15:04 Swedish time): middleware logs per-request shape (entry count, per-position class labels, peer class, booleans, distinct-value counts under a per-process HMAC key); GET /v1/debug/xff-shape returns the same for the caller's own request. Read via the Railway connector (deploy logs, filter xff-shape) and by calling the endpoint from the orchestrator's cloud container (rotating egress).

own_probe_calls.shape: entry_count 2, entry_classes [public_v4, public_v4], peer_class cgnat, left_most_is_peer false, every call
own_probe_calls.forged_header_call: Request sent with 'X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.7, 10.0.0.1' and 'X-Real-IP: 203.0.113.9' arrived with entry_count 2 and entry_classes [public_v4, public_v4]: the client-supplied header was replaced, not appended to (an append would have produced 4 entries including a private class).

corroborating_evidence.pre_incident_identity: Under the old left-most rule, each request's ipHash equalled sha256 of the caller's own egress IP (4 distinct callers matched), recorded in the incident doc.
corroborating_evidence.incident_identity: Under the right-most rule (#910), 9 requests from >=5 distinct egress IPs collapsed to 2 identities, i.e. the right-most entry is Railway's edge, served from a pool (9 distinct right-most values over 200 real requests).

raw.conclusion: Production X-Forwarded-For is exactly '<client>, <railway-edge-public-ip>' (2 entries, both public IPv4), written by Railway's edge, which discards any client-supplied value. The client is the left-most entry, equivalently the second entry from the right. The socket peer is a CGNAT-range internal proxy. X-Real-IP is also present; CF-Connecting-IP and Forwarded are not.
raw.implication_for_wp12_batch4: A trusted-hop rule must take the entry ONE hop left of the edge: client = entries[len-2] when len >= 2 (TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS counts Railway's edge as one appended hop). The current left-most rule is correct today because Railway overwrites; the hardened rule only adds safety if Railway ever starts appending. Retry the identity probe before merge from a stable-egress machine.
raw.privacy: No address, hash or port was logged or returned; 0 of 200 lines contained an IPv4-like substring.
